claims.claim: Original 650 Watts, 144 cell, Canadian brand solar panel
claims.evidence: No nameplate, sticker, or rating label is visible in photo 0 to confirm wattage, cell count, or brand.

claims.claim: Used solar panel, 'built to serve u'
claims.evidence: Panels appear used/weathered in photo 0, but no electrical test (voltage/current under sun) is shown.

claims.claim: Battery is new, holds charge for 8 hours, never repaired
claims.evidence: No battery appears anywhere in photo 0; the claim cannot be matched to any item in the image.

risks.risk: Actual wattage/brand may be much lower than claimed (650W Canadian is a premium, high-price item; without a label this could be a generic lower-wattage poly panel).
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the panel's rear nameplate/sticker showing brand, wattage, Voc/Isc/Vmp/Imp.
risks.if_unproven: Cannot be priced even at worst case, since wattage is the primary price driver and no comparable range can be safely assumed.

risks.risk: Panel output may be degraded (cracked cells, hot spots, broken bypass diodes) from prior use.
risks.proof: A video of the panel connected to a multimeter/clamp meter in direct sunlight showing voltage and current readings.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as non-functional/worst case until shown working.

risks.risk: The 'new battery, 8-hour backup' claim refers to an item not shown in any photo; it may not exist, be unrelated, or be in poor condition.
risks.proof: A photo of the actual battery with its label (brand, Ah, voltage) plus a photo/video of a charge-discharge test or receipt.
risks.if_unproven: Battery claim excluded from valuation entirely; if bundled, priced as absent/non-functional until proven.

risks.risk: Stock/generic photo reuse (shop watermark 'NAGOTECH SOLAR') suggests the image may be a catalog shot rather than the specific unit being sold.
risks.proof: A fresh photo of the exact panel(s) for sale, taken outdoors in current condition, without watermark, alongside today's date/newspaper for proof of possession.
risks.if_unproven: Treated as unverified identity of the specific unit; priced conservatively as a generic used panel of unknown wattage.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the panel's rear nameplate/rating sticker (brand, wattage, cell count, Voc/Isc).
Video of the panel under sunlight connected to a multimeter showing actual voltage/current output.
Photo of the claimed battery with its label and a charge/discharge test or recent receipt.
A fresh, un-watermarked photo of the specific unit for sale with proof of current possession (e.g., handwritten note with date).
response.reason: The photo shows unlabeled panels with no visible wattage, cell count, or brand marking, and the claimed battery is not shown at all, so no worst-case price can be anchored without the nameplate or further proof.
